complexity_matrix.operation: BFS or DFS traversal with an adjacency list
complexity_matrix.notes: V vertices plus E edges. Both terms necessary: an edgeless graph still costs O(V), a dense one is edge-dominated.

complexity_matrix.operation: Lower bound on any traversal reading an adjacency list
complexity_matrix.notes: A vertex with unexamined incident edges cannot be classified as connected or not, so every vertex and every edge must be read. BFS and DFS attain it.

complexity_matrix.operation: Same traversal with an adjacency matrix
complexity_matrix.notes: Processing each vertex scans its whole row regardless of degree. Better only when E is genuinely dense.
V extractions at O(log V) plus O(E) relaxations. Requires non-negative weights; unsound otherwise.

complexity_matrix.operation: Dijkstra shortest path, array version or dense graph
complexity_matrix.notes: Linear scan for the minimum instead of a heap. Wins only when E is a constant fraction of V^2.
V-1 passes relaxing every edge. The extra factor over Dijkstra is the price of tolerating negative weights.
Dense-graph method, O(V) per source. The best known unconditional all-pairs bound.
Same Theta(V+E) tightness argument as traversal. Requires a DAG; a cycle is detected when no zero-in-degree vertex remains.
Near-linear. Below 5 operations per element for any practical V, so effectively linear.
One DFS pass using low-link values and a stack of unfinished vertices. Tight by the traversal bound.
A back edge in the DFS forest is detected exactly when a cycle exists. No separate bound from traversal.

complexity_matrix.operation: Building the adjacency list from an edge list
complexity_matrix.notes: One bucket append per edge plus V bucket initialisations. The graph must exist before any traversal runs.

correctness_argument.claim: A traversal visits exactly the vertices reachable from the source: safety holds by induction on iterations, since extending a path along an edge to a reached vertex reaches a reached vertex; completeness holds by induction along any path, since processing each visited vertex enqueues every unvisited neighbour.

cost_derivations.claim: Traversal costs Theta(V + E) — each vertex enqueued once, each edge examined once per direction — and Omega(V + E) is a matching lower bound because a vertex with unexamined incident edges cannot be classified as connected or not, so every vertex and edge must be read.
cost_derivations.detail: An adjacency matrix raises the same traversal to O(V^2), which is why the list is preferred whenever the graph is sparse.

limits.claim: The traversal bound is tight, so traversal cannot be improved; Dijkstra's non-negative-weight restriction is falsifiable rather than a limitation of effort. Conditionally on the negative-weight triangle hypothesis, no combinatorial algorithm improves O(VE) general negative-weight shortest path to O(E^(3-epsilon)).
limits.detail: No known sub-linear static algorithm exists for undirected reachability, and one would imply a breakthrough on dense triangle detection.
